insight: For Haiti, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have generally been a positive turning point, with the team gaining momentum in 5 out of 6 breaks, indicating a slight increase in performance after the pause. On average, Haiti's momentum increases by 0.133 minutes after a hydration break, suggesting that the team is able to refocus and come back stronger. However, when Haiti is pressing before a break, their momentum actually decreases, with an average decline of 0.400 minutes per break, and they have been unable to regain their footing after the pause. In contrast, when Haiti is not pressing before a break, they tend to maintain or gain momentum, with an average increase of 0.240 minutes per break, highlighting the importance of strategic breaks in their gameplay.
